repro: askMap({ text:null, plan:null, prev:null, context:{ incidentId:<GCC-SWM incident>, zone:null, taluk:null, ward:null, drawn:null }, user:{ role:'department_officer', lockDept:'GCC-ELE' } }) (same body as POST /api/map/ask). Probe: tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer2/p6-006-real.probe.txt (last describe; ran as tests/qa/pass4/zz-reviewer2.test.ts with QA_PIN_PORT=3197, file since deleted)

area: P6-006 / Ask District IQ news lane (officer lock)
title: An officer's news answers carry other departments' incident ids, status, severity, deaths and place
where: chennai-grievance-portal-main/src/lib/assistant/fastpath.ts:610 and :624 (topStories with no dept; selectedIncidentId = matched incident), src/lib/assistant/news.ts:176-180
repro: As officer GCC-ELE: 'top news this week', then (same session) 'tell me more about the first one'. Probe: p6-006-real.probe.txt, describe 'news'
evidence: 6 stories matched to POL-GCP / DIST-DM incidents (e.g. INC-20261105-DDD4E8): matchedIncidentId, department 'Greater Chennai Police', location = incident place_text, whyRelevant 'Linked to a high-severity incident', '4 deaths reported', 'Still open'; the follow-up news_detail keeps INC-20261105-DDD4E8 in card and context. evidence/reviewer2/p6-006-news.json

Before ebe5810 a cross-department match was never sameProblem, so no button.

title: Tamil lines with no Tamil stop words: one shared filler word ('எங்கள்', 'தெருவில்', 'பகுதியில்') makes two different problems 'the same problem', with an attach offered
where: chennai-grievance-portal-main/src/lib/manu/repeat.ts:18-21 (STOP is English only), :34 (samePerson needs one shared word)
evidence: sameTopic('எங்கள் தெருவில் தெரு விளக்கு எரியவில்லை','எங்கள் தெருவில் சாக்கடை அடைப்பு', true) = true; drinking water vs sewage block from the same person: "This is this person's second petition on this problem..." and attachTo INC-W-2026-111AAA.
cause: words() now keeps Tamil letters, but the English-only STOP list and the one-word rule for the same person were tuned for English; Tamil possessives/locatives are never dropped.

title: The same person's online complaint in another department matches on one shared word: 'Water stagnation on the road' (SWD) = 'Drinking water not supplied' (Metrowater)
evidence: headline: "This is this person's second petition on this problem. The last one was filed on 12.09.2026 and is still open."
cause: For samePerson + online the department no longer gates the topic and sameTopic(samePerson) needs only one shared content word.

title: With a street typed the contradiction is never checked: same name + a common street name in ANOTHER ward with ANOTHER mobile on both sides is still 'this person'
evidence: R. Kumar, 'Gandhi Street', ward 70, mobile 9000011111 vs R. Kumar, '5, Gandhi Street, Adyar', ward 176, mobile 9444400000: samePerson true.
cause: `street ? streetIn(...) : !contradicts`: the ward/mobile contradiction applies only when no street is typed; Chennai street names (Gandhi Street, Main Road, 2nd Street) repeat in every ward.

title: Numbered streets match each other: '3rd Street' = '2nd Street', '4th Cross Street' = '5th Cross Street' (now against every part of the address)
evidence: Both samePerson true (similarity 0.78 and 0.94 >= 0.7). Before the fix the fuzzy match only hit when the street ended the address; streetIn() applies it to every comma part.
cause: Levenshtein ratio 0.7 on short squashed strings: one digit/ordinal differs.

title: One neighbour who wrote once with a mobile and once without is '2 other people'
evidence: headline '2 other people have written about this in the same ward.' for one name.
cause: who = mobile || name: the same person gets a mobile key on one petition and a name key on the other.

title: A zero-width non-joiner inside a Tamil word splits it in words() (squash() drops it), so the same word is not shared
cause: \p{Cf} is replaced by a space instead of removed.

title: The petition the headline names ('the last one was filed on …') can be outside the 4 rows the desk shows (pre-existing)
evidence: 5 newer other-problem petitions push 2026-SEW (named in the headline) out of matches[0..3].
cause: Rows are sorted by date across all kinds; same-problem rows are not put first.

title: pdfImages' dictionary regex is quadratic: a 120 KB crafted PDF takes 3.3 s, a 1 MB one minutes, blocking the event loop
evidence: One dictionary '<< ' + '/Subtype/Image '.repeat(k) + '>>' with no stream: 30 KB 256 ms, 60 KB 938 ms, 120 KB 3342 ms (x3.6 per doubling); 15 MB (upload limit) extrapolates to hours. Reached by Studio's scan path and the Manu desk's PDF pages (files.ts:33).
cause: Lazy groups around '/Subtype /Image': with k occurrences and no '>> stream' the engine retries each occurrence and rescans to the end of the dictionary (O(k*L)). Not touched by a3937ca.

title: /Length 12 0 R (indirect, object number >= 10) is read as /Length 1: a JPEG page is cut to 1 byte (no note), a Flate page is skipped
evidence: DCT stream with /Length 12 0 R: images[0].length 1 (expected 313); Flate grey page with /Length 12 0 R: { images:0, skipped:1 }. /Length 5 0 R works (control).
cause: In /\/Length\s+(\d+)(?!\s+\d+\s+R)/ the \d+ backtracks to '1' so the negative lookahead passes. Streaming PDF writers (scanners) use indirect lengths. Pre-existing.

title: A 762 KB PDF makes pdfImages hold 600 MB (15 x 40 Mpx), then OCR runs on fifteen 40 Mpx pages; per request, with no global cap
evidence: { fileKB:762, images:15, skipped:5, heldMB:600, ms:1847 }: 768x amplification (P5-028's 150 MB budget allowed 4x less).
cause: Budget raised to fit 20 real A4 300 dpi pages; it is per call, so a few concurrent uploads exceed memory. A per-page pixel cap or downscale before OCR would serve real scans.

title: A /Length too large (but inside the file) on one page now silently swallows the next page
evidence: 2 JPEG pages, page 1's /Length overshoots into page 2: images 1, skipped 0 (before a3937ca the regex resumed after the dictionary and found page 2).
cause: re.lastIndex jumps to start+Length with no check that 'endstream' is there.

title: Flate pages with an ICCBased/indirect colour space are left out, and a JPEG page with an SMask counts as two pages (pre-existing)
evidence: RGB Flate page with /ColorSpace 7 0 R: 0 images; JPEG + SMask: 2 images for one page.
cause: Only /DeviceRGB and /DeviceGray are read; any 8-bit grey image (a soft mask included) is taken as a page.
